summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded systems and firmware experience across STM32 bare-metal C, FreeRTOS, and interrupt-driven peripheral control (UART/I2C/SPI/ADC/GPIO). Built real-time embedded pipelines integrating sensors, actuators, and wireless links on STM32, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi, validated on oscilloscopes and logic analyzers. Comfortable owning firmware end to end, from register-level drivers through PCB bring-up and system integration.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, interfacing ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over I2C and streaming 3-DoF motion data via HC-05 Bluetooth to translate gestures into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding in embedded C; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback for national-level competitions.
Led a 25-member robotics team end to end across mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware/AI integration.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in bare-metal embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display, with no HAL or RTOS abstraction.
Programmed peripherals directly at the register level (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1): timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified timing and signal integrity in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Built a real-time embedded control system on STM32 with FreeRTOS, using mutex-protected shared memory for task coordination between sensing, control, and display tasks.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control driven by interrupt-driven UART commands from a Jetson-based vision front end, with a manual user override path.
Integrated VL53L0X time-of-flight sensing over I2C with OLED distance visualization for closed-loop targeting.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built the embedded control layer of a distributed pick-and-place robot: two-link IK in C++ on Arduino driving five servos, with dual VL53L0X ToF sensors muxed over I2C via TCA9548A for contact-aware grasping at 25mm.
Designed interrupt-driven serial command handling between the Jetson vision pipeline and Arduino motion controller over a WebSocket-to-UART bridge.
Root-caused 11 field integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) via oscilloscope/logic analyzer traces; reached 100% pick reliability (10/10) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
